title: Power Rankings: Heat start off on top with West trio not far behind
heading: 2006-07 Power Rankings: Training Camp
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: Why wouldn't my Heat get the same treatment every defending champ gets from the committee (of one)? They start on top and shame on you for suspecting otherwise.
rankings.summaryText: Why wouldn't my Heat get the same treatment every defending champ gets from the committee (of one)? They start on top and shame on you for suspecting otherwise.

rankings.summaryHtml: On paper, Mavs are even deeper than they were. But they still have to keep Nowitzki fresh, cope with the brutal West and prove they can get over their Finals heartache.
rankings.summaryText: On paper, Mavs are even deeper than they were. But they still have to keep Nowitzki fresh, cope with the brutal West and prove they can get over their Finals heartache.

rankings.summaryHtml: Tell me you're not buying this Spurs Are Slipping stuff. Don't forget they won 63 games last season playing more small ball than they've ever played before.

rankings.summaryHtml: If we knew what to expect from Amare -- and if it's good news -- Suns would be my pick to win it all. They still might be, but I'll need October to scout it out.

rankings.summaryHtml: Wrenching as it was to lose Darko and Big Ben in a five-month span, Detroit still ranks no worse than No. 2 in a weakened (at the top) East in spite of that No. 11 summer.

rankings.summaryHtml: Skeptics will say Bulls haven't even won a playoff series yet. My counter: Chicago played Miami tougher than anyone in the East and just added Ben, P.J. and more.
rankings.summaryText: Skeptics will say Bulls haven't even won a playoff series yet. My counter: Chicago played Miami tougher than anyone in the East and just added Ben, P.J. and more.

rankings.summaryHtml: Cavs have proven they're East top-four material. But Bulls look stronger from here unless Hughes makes a splashy return or LBJ can carry even more of the load.

rankings.summaryHtml: Clips came within one win of the West finals and bring back almost the exact same team. Still trying to work out which of those developments is more extraordinary.
rankings.summaryText: Clips came within one win of the West finals and bring back almost the exact same team. Still trying to work out which of those developments is more extraordinary.

rankings.summaryHtml: Signing a desperate Bonzi on the cheap? Had to do it. Now can T-Mac and Yao stay healthy? Had to ask . . . no matter how much better their supporting cast looks.

rankings.summaryHtml: What stuns me even more than Hornets' first-ever summer splash are all the negative reactions. Would another summer of non-spending have been better?

rankings.summaryHtml: A year ago, Rod Thorn said J-Kidd's Nets were deeper than ever. No one's even pretending to say so now about a small, thin crew at risk for exiting the East elite.

rankings.summaryHtml: Remember how we picked Lakers to make the playoffs just because Phil was back? In this West, Phil and Kobe might have to have better years just to keep them there.

rankings.summaryHtml: Still not totally sure which seven West teams will finish below Warriors. But that's Nellie's problem. I only made the playoff guarantee; it's his job to live up to it.

rankings.summaryHtml: The roster looks better and so does 'Melo, but the concerns haven't changed: Nuggets need shooters and (uh-oh) need Furious George and K-Mart to co-exist somehow.

rankings.summaryHtml: If Jazz miss the playoffs again, that would be four straight trips to the lottery. Tough to imagine Jerry Sloan going out that way, but the West could well be that brutal.

rankings.summaryHtml: Clutch as it was to snare Harrington, starting fast would be one of our man Carlisle's best tricks yet, given that Pacers have to work in, oh, about 10 new faces.

rankings.summaryHtml: Praise for the Charlie V. trade was nearly unanimous. But Stotts' seat is warming, as he'll be expected to do more with a more mobile frontcourt.

rankings.summaryHtml: No one expects tiny Wiz to challenge Miami for the division title. But we do demand a big rebound from Arenas after his FT playoff nightmare and Team USA snip.

rankings.summaryHtml: Funny thing about all that great press Magic received last April. Now Dwight and Darko -- Dwight especially after talking Orlando up even louder -- have to live up to it.

rankings.summaryHtml: Last season's 33-49 slog was Wolves' worst season since KG's rookie mark of 26-56. But he was on the rise back then. Now even KG admits: "Clock is ticking, man."

rankings.summaryHtml: There will be questions -- lots -- about Muss and Artest, but the bigger red flags to me remain (A) replacing Bonzi with Salmons and (B) the absence of further tweaks.

rankings.summaryHtml: Can this really be Ainge's fourth season in charge? Perhaps it's not just Ainge's coach and all his kiddies who are due to pick it up a notch.

rankings.summaryHtml: The two questions being asked in many languages: How long will it take for all these worldly newcomers to settle and mesh? And how long will Sam get to coach them?

rankings.summaryHtml: Hawks are still my favorite bad team to watch, but that's strictly because of the on-the-rise lefty (Josh) and Joe. (Yes, Marvin, that's us trying to get a rise out of you.)
